questions.stem: In the two-link diagram, which assignment matches the frame origins and x-axis directions?
assumptions: Use the frame assignment drawn in this source example, not an arbitrary alternative convention.

options.text: Frames0 and1 originate at the base, with x0 horizontal and x1 along link1; frame2 originates at the elbow with x2 along link2, and frame3 is at the tip aligned with frame2
Frame1 originates at the elbow along link1; frame2 is at the tip along link2; frame3 is at the base

Frame1 originates at the base along link1; frame2 is at the elbow but its x2 remains horizontal, and frame3 points along link1

solution.justification: The drawn axes and the offsets P_C1=l1 x1 and P_C2=l2 x2 locate the link-attached frames at the proximal joints, with the terminal frame at the second tip.

optionExplanations.o1: This matches the complete geometry and both center-of-mass offsets.

optionExplanations.o3: The diagram shows elbow and tip origins distinct from the base.
optionExplanations.o4: The second-link frame is aligned with link2 rather than remaining base-horizontal.

questions.stem: The source notes that even a2-DOF closed-form torque equation is lengthy; why can the recursive method still be useful for a6-DOF robot?
questions.subtopic: Long symbolic equations do not prevent recursive evaluation

options.text: It first requires every joint torque to be expanded into a closed-form symbolic expression before any numerical evaluation
It shortens the computation by treating each link as dynamically uncoupled from its neighbours
It avoids the long expressions by dropping velocity-product terms while retaining only acceleration and gravity terms
It evaluates linkwise motion and force recursions without requiring a fully expanded symbolic torque formula

•  Expressions for the torque at the actuators 𝜏1 and 𝜏2 are function
   of joint position, velocity, and acceleration.
•  Note that these complex expressions are for one of the simplest
   manipulators imaginable (2 DOF planar).
•  Obviously, the closed-form equations for a manipulator with 6
  DOF will be quite complex.

citations.locator: Lecture 13, physical PDF page 425, printed slide 22: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
Summary

•  The complete algorithm for computing joint
   torques from the motion of the joints is
  composed of two parts.
•  First, link velocities and accelerations are
   iteratively computed from link 1 out to link 𝑛
  and the Newton—Euler equations are applied
   to each link.
•  Second, for given forces and torques of
   interaction at EE, joint actuator torques are
  computed recursively from link 𝑛 back to link 1.

solution.justification: The warning concerns the size of explicitly expanded expressions; the two-pass algorithm can evaluate the same dynamics through local intermediate quantities.

optionExplanations.o1: This distinguishes symbolic expression size from recursive numerical evaluation.
optionExplanations.o2: The linkwise numerical recursions do not require full symbolic expansion first.
optionExplanations.o3: Outward motion propagation and inward force propagation retain coupling between links.
optionExplanations.o4: The exact recursions include velocity-product effects; neglecting them would be an additional approximation.
